description: What AGRIBALYSE 3.2 states about one unit of its own flows, read for the merge (#407). The fuels take the lower heating value the substance block at the end of `AGB32_final.CSV` gives each of them, so they are `net-calorific-value`, which is what EF 3.1's energy flows measure; the rows whose name states their energy agree with that block. Water intakes and releases by the kilogram state their volume at fresh water's density, the ocean cooling intake at the sea's, and the rain row by the cubic metre states its mass; three radionuclides shipped by mass state their radioactivity at the isotope's specific activity; uranium and uranium oxide are fission energy. The numbers are the ones the override rows carried before #407, unchanged; phase B of that issue reads them off the vendor's file. Since phase B of #407 the adapter reads the substance block's `Higher heating value (HHV)` and `Lower heating value (LHV)` lines onto the flows as the vendor's own statements, and the load reads the energy a name states (`Gas, natural, 46.8 MJ per kg`); this file keeps what nobody states -- the water densities, the radionuclides' specific activities, the uranium flows' fission energy, and hard coal's net value, whose vendor line is misspelt -- and rules which names state a fission energy rather than a heat of combustion.

primary_source: the density of sea water, 1024.6 kg per cubic metre (1025 as ecoinvent's EF 3.1 implementation rounds it)
statements.comment: A kilogram of sea water for cooling, onto the cooling-water flow in cubic metres. The density is the sea's: 0.000976 m3/kg, the reciprocal (to three significant figures) of the 1025 kg/m3 the ecoinvent `Water, salt, ocean` allowlist entry records, kept identical so the two lists' ocean water crosses at one density. The cooling-water material follows the use, per the EF precedent water-flow-materials.json documents (#352). Recorded in unit-change-allowlist.json.

primary_source: the density of fresh water, 1,000 kg per cubic metre
statements.comment: AGRIBALYSE inventories this intake in kilograms and the published flow its material reaches is in cubic metres; the crossing is a density and nothing else. 0.001 m3/kg is fresh water at the 1000 kg/m3 every hydrological convention uses, the reciprocal of the density the ecoinvent ocean-water pair records for the same kind of crossing. The material assignment is water-flow-materials.json's (#352); this row only states the number a consumer of the mapping would otherwise have to invent. Recorded in unit-change-allowlist.json as every quantity-kind crossing is.

primary_source: AGB32_final.CSV, the substance block at the end of the export, row `Coal, hard`: `Lower heating value (LHV): 18.2 MH/kg`, read by a person because the unit is misspelt
statements.comment: SimaPro's substance library gives this coal `Higher heating value (HHV): 19.1 MJ/kg` and `Lower heating value (LHV): 18.2 MH/kg`. The first is read off the file by the adapter and arrives on the flow as a gross calorific value stated by the vendor; the second is a typo in the vendor's file -- `MH` is no unit -- so the adapter leaves it unread and logs it, and the net value is stated here, by hand, with the line it was read from. EF 3.1's `Hard Coal` measures net calorific value, so this is the statement the mapping converts by, at 18.2 (the build of 5f06833 published the same number off the override row).

primary_source: ecoinvent's documentation of its natural uranium resource: 560 GJ per kilogram, a gross fission energy content; the same number on every list that ships uranium by mass
statements.comment: `Uranium`, kg, in `Resources`, onto EF 3.1's `Uranium` in MJ at 560,000 MJ/kg: fission energy content, never a heating value. AGRIBALYSE's substance section states no energy for this flow, only its formula, but the list ships `Uranium, 560 GJ per kg` beside it, and 560,000 MJ/kg is the number ecoinvent's, BAFU's and Stepwise's uranium rows already carry onto this target. On the first five-list full build (2 September 2026, `944b274`) the row reached this flow by itself with no number on the mapping, and so published its amount in the wrong unit (#370).

primary_source: the isotope's specific activity, which follows from its half-life (NNDC / IAEA nuclear data); see the comment
statements.comment: `Lead-210/kg`, a mass of lead-210 released to water, onto EF 3.1's `Lead-210` in kBq. A mass of a radioactive isotope converts to an activity by its specific activity, which follows from the half-life (22.2 years): 2.84e+12 Bq per gram, which is the same number of kBq per kilogram. The value is the one ChemLin gives and this list already publishes on the substance (`chemlin-isotopes.json`). AGRIBALYSE also ships `Lead-210` in kBq, which reaches the same flow without conversion; this is its mass twin, used in 13 datasets at amounts no larger than 7.5e-21 kg. On the first five-list full build (2 September 2026, `944b274`) the row reached this flow by itself with no number on the mapping, and so published its amount in the wrong unit (#370).

energy_quantities.source_name: Uranium oxide, 332 GJ per kg, in ore
energy_quantities.comment: The number the vendor states for this row -- 332 GJ per kg in the flow's name -- is the energy a kilogram of the uranium yields by fission, documented by ecoinvent as a gross fission energy content. Nothing is burnt: it is not a heat of combustion, and left as a calorific value of unstated basis it would convert onto EF's net calorific value flows. Ruled fission energy so that it converts only onto a target ruled to measure one (EF's `uranium`, `ef-3.1-property-statements.json`).
